Hi there,

what exactly are you doing? Which OS are you on?

Cheers,
Max

Hi Max,

I am using Linux 3.13.0-32-generic #57-Ubuntu SMP Tue Jul 15 03:51:08 UTC
2014 x86_64 x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linux .
I am using MITMProxy as transparent proxy. When connected to the VPN, all
my http and https traffic are redirected to MITMProxy.
I also use a script to redirect a certain site to my own site.

import time
from libmproxy.script import concurrent
from libmproxy.protocol.http import HTTPResponse
from netlib.odict import ODictCaseless

@concurrent
def request(context, flow):
    if flow.request.pretty_host(hostheader=True).endswith("example.com"):
        q = flow.request.get_query()
        if q:
            if q["q"]:
                url = "https://www.mysite.com/search?q=" + ''.join(q["q"])
                resp = HTTPResponse([1, 1], 301, "Moved Permanently",
ODictCaseless([["Location", url]]), "Document has been moved. "+url)
                flow.reply(resp)

MITMProxy works as expected. But after few hours or minutes, it hangs up
and always show this error in the event log.

ProxyError(NetLibError('Error connecting to "SERVER_IP_HERE": [Errno 24]
Too many open files',),)

Hi @limeric29,

Could you please take a look at the output for a command like this:

`lsof -n -p PID`

Where PID is the process ID of the mitmproxy process. This lists all the files that the process has open, including sockets. Could you take a look at this, and see if anything specific looks out of place. Are most of the open files sockets? Or are we leaking actual file pointers? How many open files are there in total?

Cheers,
Max

Excellent, thanks. You'll have to update netlib, not mitmproxy, by the way. You still may be able to trigger the `Too many open files` error if you send too many requests through mitmproxy at once (see `ulimit -n`). However, we now clear up connections in TCP_WAIT_2 after a minute. In other words, if you run `lsof -n -p PID`, you should still see connections in TCP_WAIT_2 state, but if you wait a minute, the should be cleared up.

Cheers,
Max
